title: Spot queue specs must clean up the Kanbus tasks they create
description:
The `features/03_spot_queue.feature` steps create real Kanbus tasks on every
run and never remove them, so each `behave` run leaves spec scaffolding on the
board labeled `spot:cursor` and `spot:antigravity.gemini`.

This directly violates the invariant in story `5f632d` -- *open Kanbus chores
labeled spot are the only backlog*. A spot worker searching for work by label
picks up fake chores.

## Current litter

| Label | Rows | Spec-generated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spot:cursor` | 19 | 15 (titles ending in a unix timestamp) |
| `spot:antigravity.gemini` | 6 | 5 (titles ending in a unix timestamp) |

## Definition of Done

- The `a Kanbus task is labeled` and `the following tasks are labeled` steps
  record every created id on the behave context.
- `features/environment.py` `after_scenario` deletes those ids, the same way it
  already deletes the `04_claude_dispatch` chore via `spec_task_id`.
- Existing timestamped litter is deleted with `kbs delete <id> --yes`.
  Untimestamped rows are left alone -- they are not provably spec output.
- `.venv/bin/behave` stays green at 4 features / 13 scenarios, and
  `.venv/bin/pytest` stays green.
- `kbs list --label spot:cursor` and `--label spot:antigravity.gemini` return
  only real work afterwards.

## Cleanup lifecycle

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as spot queue step
    participant K as Kanbus
    participant E as after_scenario
    S->>K: kbs create "Task A <ts>" --label spot:cursor
    S->>K: kbs list --label spot:cursor --porcelain
    K-->>S: id
    S->>S: context.spec_task_ids.append(id)
    Note over S,E: scenario ends
    E->>K: kbs delete <id> --yes
```

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Implementation

**Steps** (`features/steps/steps.py`): added `_create_spec_task(context, title, label, priority=None)`,
which creates the task and records its Kanbus id on `context.spec_task_ids` in the
same call. Both spot queue steps -- `a Kanbus task is labeled` and
`the following tasks are labeled` -- now go through it, so a create can no longer
happen without a matching record. The id comes from `kbs list --label <label>
--porcelain` filtered on the unique timestamped title, the same lookup the
`04_claude_dispatch` chore step already uses.

**Teardown** (`features/environment.py`): `after_scenario` now iterates
`_spec_task_ids(context)`, which merges the list from the spot queue steps with the
single `spec_task_id` the dispatch specs still need to pass to the worker stub as
`SPEC_TASK_ID`, de-duplicated. Both shapes are deleted with `kbs delete <id> --yes`.

## Purge

Deleted 20 leftover issues, every one matching
`(Task A|Task B|Task C|Gemini Only Task) <unix timestamp>`:

- `spot:cursor` (15): 0d32f2 25e955 28cd04 5ac504 625140 7e8e63 85e1bf ab18bf
  b62bbd bad448 c5238c d1969b d23c67 d4da52 d72d8b
- `spot:antigravity.gemini` (5): 1cc531 1f8e9c 2cf4c6 9d27aa ca7af3

The timestamp suffix was re-checked per row at delete time, not just when the list
was built.

## Verification

- `.venv/bin/behave` -- 4 features, 13 scenarios, 71 steps passed.
- `.venv/bin/pytest` -- 40 passed.
- Ran behave twice. Label counts were identical before and after each run, so the
  specs now create and reclaim their own tasks.

## Left alone

Five untimestamped rows do not match the spec-output criterion and were not
touched: `4ef0d9` Task B (closed), `aec077` Task C (closed), `e7113e` Task A
(closed), `36756c` Gemini Only Task (closed), `5c847e` Test task for search (open).
They look like pre-timestamp spec residue but cannot be proven to be, so they are
left for a human call.
